title: Imputed Righteousness
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Imputed righteousness means that the righteousness of Christ is counted to believers by faith. The believer’s right standing before God rests on Christ’s righteousness, not personal merit or spiritual performance.
summary: Imputed righteousness means that the righteousness of Christ is counted to believers by faith. The believer’s right standing before God rests on Christ’s righteousness, not personal merit or spiritual performance.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the righteous One who stands for His people. Through union with Him, sinners receive a righteousness they did not produce and could never earn.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Imputation means that God counts or credits righteousness to the believer. This doctrine is closely tied to justification because God declares sinners righteous in Christ.

The believer does not stand before God clothed in self-made righteousness. Even the best human obedience cannot erase sin or satisfy the standard of God’s holiness.

Christ obeyed perfectly and gave Himself for sinners. In Him, believers receive a righteousness from God that is by faith, not a righteousness of their own.

This truth magnifies grace. The believer is accepted not because God lowers His standard, but because Christ fulfills righteousness and gives His people a secure standing before God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many Christians live as though their standing rises and falls with their daily performance. When they do well, they feel acceptable; when they fail, they feel cast out. Imputed righteousness anchors them in Christ.

This doctrine also guards against pride. The mature believer and the struggling believer stand before God only in the righteousness of Jesus. No one graduates beyond grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in the righteousness of Christ. Pursue holiness, but do not confuse your growth with the ground of your acceptance. When accused by guilt or tempted by pride, return to the truth that your standing before God is in Jesus, not in yourself.
